title: Importance of Trade in Islam
summary: Trade is vital in Islam, emphasizing earning through lawful means as a duty.
translation: In Islam, trade holds great significance and is considered so important that earning lawful income is regarded as one of the essential obligations. Fulfilling rights is obligatory on every person, and when something is obligatory, utilizing the means to achieve it also becomes obligatory. Therefore, activities like farming, employment, industry, and trade are all means to earn lawful income. A truthful and trustworthy trader is given glad tidings of being with the prophets. Likewise, it has been said that a nation that does not engage in trade and does not strive for lawful earning eventually loses its culture and identity. Therefore, following the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) includes trade, which was a special means of livelihood for the righteous predecessors and a source of blessings in sustenance. It is also the best means for the invitation and propagation of Islam. Hence, Muslims should elevate their economic status and devise some effective solutions to address economic challenges. In the same way that the Hadith emphasizes the virtue of lawful earning and trade, the Quran also contains guidance on earning, where the encouragement of striving in the cause of Allah is mentioned alongside traveling for livelihood. In Surah Muzzammil, it is stated that just as Allah subjugated the heavens and the earth for His servants, all these things are so because Allah has made the day a means of livelihood, and every living being’s sustenance is linked to humans in some way. Therefore, the Quran refers to the effort in earning livelihood as 'the favor of Allah,' implying the importance of earning one’s rightful share. It is also termed as 'Allah's embellishment,' warning against considering lawful earning as a disgrace. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was also addressed to show that despite reaching the highest level of spirituality, one cannot disregard or neglect the means of economic benefit. Therefore, today, it is necessary to address the shortcomings and weaknesses of Muslims in trade. From our predecessors and the teachings of the prophets (peace be upon them), we should certainly gauge how they intensely invested in their trade while striving for both religious and worldly success.
